title: TrueMapData: one format for measured surfaces

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A microscope measures a surface down to tiny bumps. How do you reuse that in a game engine or a lab report?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's TrueMapData, a Python library and command line tool Antoine maintains under ETSim.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Height maps from TrueMap and GelSight scanners, as NumPy arrays. So one representation serves both metrology and graphics.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What can you do with it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Export normal maps, displacement maps or meshes in formats like STL, OBJ and glTF, keeping the physical scale. Measure roughness, and plot surfaces and profiles.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Given aligned scans of a worn sample, it computes bearing curves and the volume lost between frames. The written page has an example comparing two captures.
